result:
Done. I demonstrated hippocampal place cells using **DANDI:000044** (Grosmark & Buzsáki 2016, hc-11): eight bilateral silicon-probe recordings from dorsal CA1 in four rats running mazes for water reward, streamed from S3 with `remfile` so nothing was downloaded in full.

**Headline result.** In the primary session (rat Achilles, 1.6 m linear track), 82 of 120 excitatory units (68%) have a firing field that survives a per-cell circular-shift test at p < 0.01. Pooled over all eight sessions that is 322 place cells carrying 412 fields, with the per-session fraction ranging from 33% to 90%. The median field is 32 cm wide with a 7.3 Hz in-field peak, fires on 87% of the passes through it, and its odd-lap and even-lap rate maps correlate at 0.94. Bayesian decoding from held-out laps recovers the animal's position to a median error of 5.2 cm against a 47 cm chance level (3.9 to 12.6 cm across all sessions). Poisson GLMs fitted with `nemos` rule out the obvious confound: position gains 0.63 bits/spike of held-out likelihood versus 0.04 for running speed, position wins for 90% of place cells, and adding speed to a position model buys a median of 0.000 bits/spike.

**Two things worth flagging, because they changed how I built the analysis.** Raw spatial information in bits/spike turned out to be actively misleading here: the excitatory units that *fail* the place-cell test have a *higher* median raw value (1.03) than the ones that pass (0.65), because sparse firing produces noisy, spiky rate maps. The same bias defeats sparsity and in-field/out-of-field rate contrast, so I replaced my first "place cells are sparse" panel with lap-by-lap reliability, which separates the two populations cleanly (87% vs 21% of passes). Separately, the dandiset is not homogeneous the way its title suggests: three of the eight sessions use a circular maze rather than a linear track, and track length varies (1.6 m, 2 m, ~2.9 m), so bin edges and smoothing mode are derived per session from the NWB container name. The files also store the sampling *period* in the SpatialSeries `rate` field, so timestamps have to be rebuilt by hand.

**Outputs in the working directory:** `place_cell_analysis.py` (jupytext, 56 cells, verified to run end to end at exit 0), `place_cell_analysis.ipynb`, nine PNG figures (`fig00` behaviour validation through `fig08` cross-session summary), `README.md`, and four CSV result tables. The notebook is generated by `build_notebook.py` from the tested modules (`place_cell_lib.py`, `figures.py`, `run_all.py`), so there is one copy of the analysis code and the notebook cannot drift from what was actually run.
